body:
TASK-1294 cannot satisfy the pipeline it is groomed for, and the drain is burning attempts on it now — plus its method still carries the window you said you would rebind

TIME-SENSITIVE, because it is in flight: TASK-1294 just retried with cause `no-pr`, attempt 2 of 2.

THE MISMATCH. Its acceptance is "a dated report comment on this spec giving median rounds-to-merge before and after with the per-cause split". That is a comment. It is groomed `execution_mode: drain`, and the drain's phase 1 fails with NoPr when a session exits cleanly without opening a PR. So this spec can never pass phase 1 no matter how well the implementer does the work — it will burn both attempts, shelve, and loop on every requeue.

It is the same shape as the TASK-403 punt in the historical record: "a demo/marketing meta-task whose acceptance criteria require actions a headless coding implementer cannot perform ... there is no code surface here; the spec is misrouted to the headless implementer queue." Different content, identical failure.

Worth noting where it came from, because it is not carelessness: you split this OUT of TASK-1291 precisely because it is post-deployment by construction, which was right. The grooming then gave it `drain`, which is the one mode that requires a PR. The split was correct and the mode contradicts the reason for the split.

I have not changed the mode — that is disposition and it is yours. `operator` or `decide` look closer to what the work actually is, and SPIKE-83 got operator mode for a structurally similar reason: a report-shaped spec whose instrument is a person reading output.

THE SECOND THING, and I think it matters more for the result than for the routing. The description's Method still reads:

  "count SpecShelved events between its first RunStarted and its PrMerged"

You told me yesterday you had corrected that on the spec — bound the window with the STORE instead, since the aida-store git log is the authoritative time series and the Done-to-Completed transition has a real timestamp there, with shelve counts still taken from the feed. The description I just read still carries the PrMerged form. Either the correction landed somewhere else (a comment rather than the description) or it did not land.

That matters because BUG-1286 is exactly why: PrMerged is buried by trailing phase events for drain-driven specs and absent entirely for specs closed outside a drain. An implementer following the description as written would measure a window that closes for roughly one spec in five hundred and would produce a null result for mechanical reasons, then report it honestly as a null result — which your acceptance explicitly permits. That is the worst available outcome: a correct-looking negative finding about TASK-1291's value, caused by a measurement bug rather than by the change being ineffective.

Suggest confirming the description carries the store-bound method before this is driven again, whatever mode it ends up in.

Nothing else from me on it — I have not touched the spec.

Two lanes running: BUG-1277 and BUG-1299.
